feature: dual-signed sequential plugin publisher key rotation
proved: A publisher key change requires one strict certificate bound to the exact plugin ID, next sequence, and first effective semantic version.
Both the previously established Ed25519 key and the new Ed25519 key sign the same domain-separated claim, proving old-key authorization and new-key possession.

Every retained package version is checked against its key epoch, so an old key cannot sign a package at or after the rotation's effective version while explicit rollback to an exact old signed version remains available.
The complete bounded certificate chain is reverified on read, and every retained signed package in the affected plugin lineage is rehashed and signature-verified before accepting another key.
A legacy package-only IndexedDB database upgrades in place; the new package record and accepted certificate are written in one transaction to separate bounded stores.
The checked-in non-executing CLI can create a new external key and exact dual-signed certificate without placing private key material in the package or certificate.
The product accepts the certificate as an explicit optional fourth file and reports the retained rotation sequence without claiming authenticated publisher identity.
notProved: The first installed key or self-described publisher name authenticates a legal person, organization, reputation, independent review, semantic quality, or safety.
Revocation, transparency logs, trusted time, organizational enrollment, lost-old-key recovery, or protection when the compromised current private key authorizes a malicious successor.
Recovery from browser quota exhaustion, abrupt process loss during IndexedDB commit, OS-profile rollback, or malicious same-user storage modification beyond fail-closed verification.
Packaged-app restart/upgrade behavior or a physical two-install independently built third-party package rotation; current proof is headless against production TypeScript, Rust, schema, and CLI paths.
